title: walk-blocker site configuration
description: Every fact about one site. Validated and compiled on the workstation by `walk-blocker build` (ADR-0013); nothing on the node reads this file. Path-shaped values are interpolated into systemd unit lines and root-sourced shell blocks, so their character sets are deliberately narrow.

sink_path.description: An absolute path that reaches a root-write sink: no whitespace, no `%`, `$`, `;`, quotes or backticks, because the value is pasted verbatim into unit lines and sourced shell as root. Canonical form only (no `..`, `.`, `//` or trailing slash) is checked semantically.

embedded_text.description: Short human-facing text embedded in refusal messages and unit descriptions: printable, single-line, at most 80 characters, no quoting characters.

identifier.description: A bare token such as a partition, QoS, package or tool name: letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-` only.

schema_version.description: The revision of this schema the file was written against. A file written for a later revision is refused rather than half-read.

site.description: How the site names itself to the people it refuses: the strings a refusal message, a unit description and `walk-job` embed verbatim.

display_name.description: How the site names this node in refusal text and unit descriptions, for example the class of machine and its role. Embedded verbatim in generated artifacts.

docs_url.description: Where a refused user is sent for the site's own explanation of the guard and of `walk-job`. URI characters only, no whitespace.

contact.description: The help address or queue a refusal names. Embedded verbatim in refusal text.

filesystems.description: The mount policy in three tiers (ADR-0016): a compiled default from `/proc/mounts` fields, per-mount overrides here, and `walk-blocker survey` run out of band to propose them.

remote_fstypes.description: Filesystem types treated as expensive by default; glob-aware (`fuse.*`). Broad on purpose: a small remote mount is loosened with a `[[filesystems.mounts]]` override, never by narrowing this list, because the list loosens every mount at once.

remote_proxy.description: Also treat a mount as remote when its source matches `host:` or its options contain `_netdev` or `addr=`, so a remote mount of a type no list anticipated is guarded rather than walked (ADR-0016).

maxdepth_allowed.description: The global depth ceiling: a walk of an expensive mount bounded at or below this depth is allowed on every mount without a lookup. Must not exceed `depth_allowance_max`.

unscoped_depth.description: A root this many components or fewer below an expensive mount point is refused when walked unbounded; deeper roots pass. A bounded walk is a different claim and is governed by the depth ceiling instead (ADR-0007).

depth_allowance_max.description: The hard upper bound on any depth ceiling, global or per mount. A per-mount `maxdepth` above it is refused at build.

mount_table.description: The mount table the shim reads, and the only file it opens before deciding (ADR-0015). Changed only for a test fixture.

mounts.description: Per-mount overrides of the compiled default, and the only way to loosen it: a small remote export is made `cheap` here, in a diff, and nowhere else. Run `walk-blocker survey` on the node to measure and propose entries; a mount left on its default should be left there on purpose (ADR-0016).

path.description: The mount point exactly as it appears in the mount table. Unique across entries.

class.description: `expensive` guards the mount (depth ceiling, unscoped refusal, `walk-job` named); `cheap` exempts it from the mount judgement entirely.

maxdepth.description: Replaces `maxdepth_allowed` for this mount alone; bounded above by `depth_allowance_max` and only meaningful on an `expensive` mount. Raise it only after the measurement in `docs/site-config.md` (ADR-0007).

install.description: Where the payload lands on the node. Every value is a root-write target compiled into `deploy.py` as a literal (ADR-0005, ADR-0013); all of it must be on local disk, never on the filesystem under investigation.

prefix.description: The root-owned directory the shim, reaper and `walk-job` are installed under. At least two components, so a typo cannot name a system directory.

spool_dir.description: Where the reaper's audit trail is written. Local disk: a monitor that lives on what it monitors is unavailable exactly when it is needed.

audit_filename.description: The audit file's name under `spool_dir`. One record per line; readable by the person whose process is in it (ADR-0012).

unit_dir.description: Which systemd unit directory receives the reaper service and timer. Only the two administrator-owned locations are permitted.

staging_parent.description: The local, root-owned parent under which `deploy.py` stages the payload before it touches any install target, so the payload is read once before anything that can block (ADR-0006).

tool_search_path.description: The directories, in order, the installer searches to resolve the real binaries the shim wraps. Absolute entries only; the caller's own `PATH` is never consulted.

hooks.description: One table per shell whose startup file gets the hook block. Which shells appear, and which are `required`, is a census result at the site (ADR-0008).

enabled.description: Whether this shell's hook block is written at all. A disabled hook is neither written nor verified.

file.description: The system startup file the hook block is written to. Required when the hook is enabled; which file fires for `ssh host 'cmd'` is a property of the shell and its packaging (ADR-0008).

package.description: The distribution package that likely owns the hook file, so the installer can warn that the file is a managed conffile and the next upgrade may conflict with the block.

gate.description: `required` for a registered login shell at the site (the install fails if the hook cannot be proven to fire for a remote command); `best-effort` for a shell only reached by nesting (written and checked when present, never gating). Only a census of the site's shells decides this (ADR-0008).

bash.description: The bash hook. Its system rc file fires for `ssh host 'cmd'` only under the shell's own conditions, so `verify_bash_hook` proves it rather than assuming it.

enabled.description: Whether this shell's hook block is written at all. A disabled hook is neither written nor verified.

file.description: The system startup file the hook block is written to. Required when the hook is enabled; which file fires for `ssh host 'cmd'` is a property of the shell and its packaging (ADR-0008).

package.description: The distribution package that likely owns the hook file, so the installer can warn that the file is a managed conffile and the next upgrade may conflict with the block.

gate.description: `required` for a registered login shell at the site (the install fails if the hook cannot be proven to fire for a remote command); `best-effort` for a shell only reached by nesting (written and checked when present, never gating). Only a census of the site's shells decides this (ADR-0008).

zsh.description: The zsh hook. The global `zshenv` is read unconditionally, which is why this is the stronger mechanism of the two; its location differs between distribution families.

enabled.description: Whether the fish drop-in is written at all. A disabled hook is neither written nor verified.

file.description: The dedicated `conf.d` drop-in the installer generates in full; fish reads the directory unconditionally, so there is nothing to preserve or back up. Required when enabled.

gate.description: `required` if fish is a registered login shell at the site, `best-effort` if it is only ever a nested, per-user shell. Decided by census, not assumed (ADR-0008).

fish.description: The fish hook, a dedicated `conf.d` drop-in the installer owns entirely. No `package`: nothing pre-existing is modified.

trusted_binaries.description: Absolute paths of the binaries the node artifacts call as root or from the shim. Named here so nothing on the node resolves them through a `PATH` a user controls.

logger.description: Writes the shim's escape-hatch and the reconcile's hook-state records to journald under the `walk-blocker` tag.

awk.description: Used by `walk-job` and the installer for field extraction; never by the shim before it decides.

id.description: Resolves the invoking account for audit records and for `walk-job`'s output path.

date.description: Timestamps audit records outside the shim's decision path.

timeout.description: Bounds the reconcile's hook probes and the survey's per-mount measurement, so a wedged filesystem cannot hang either.

sh.description: The POSIX shell the shim and `walk-job` run under. Must be dash-clean at the site (ADR-0015).

python3.description: The interpreter the reaper and `deploy.py` run under; stdlib-only Python 3.9 is the floor (ADR-0015).

bfs.description: An optional breadth-first `find` the refusal text may recommend for shallow, wide trees. Wrapped only when named here and resolvable at install.

slurm.description: How `walk-job` submits a traversal the shim refused (ADR-0007). The bound moves from depth to wall clock, and the scheduler enforces it.

partition.description: The partition `walk-job` submits to. A small, low-priority partition is expected; its default wall clock is what bounds one user's long walk.

qos.description: The QoS `walk-job` submits under, so its jobs never preempt tenant work.

account.description: An accounting association to charge `walk-job` submissions to, if the site requires one.

default_time.description: The wall-clock limit `walk-job` requests when the user gives none, in the scheduler's `[D-]HH[:MM[:SS]]` form. Kept low so raising it is a visible choice.

default_mem.description: The memory `walk-job` requests when the user gives none. Load-bearing: a partition with an unlimited default charges the whole node to a job that names no memory (ADR-0007).

sbatch_glob.description: An absolute path or glob that resolves to the scheduler's `sbatch`; a glob accommodates a versioned install prefix. Resolved at run time by `walk-job`, never through the user's `PATH`.

nice.description: The scheduler nice value `walk-job` submits with, so a traversal yields to every other job in the partition.

output_pattern.description: The output file name `walk-job` passes to the scheduler, using the scheduler's own `%` substitutions. Written in the submitting directory.

min_job_age_s.description: How old a scheduler job must be before the reaper attributes a traversal to it rather than to a login session; a very young job is more likely a login-node preamble.

extra_job_tools.description: Site-local job-triage commands the refusal text names alongside the accounting query when a scheduler job token appears in argv.

shim.description: Layer 1 knobs. The shim is advisory by design (ADR-0001): everything here shapes what it wraps, not what it can enforce.

unwrapped_tools.description: Tools in the rule table the site chooses not to wrap, typically interactive finders whose own walk is bounded by the user's attention. Listed by name; the table stays generic.

reaper.description: Layer 2, the periodic backstop. It scans and classifies the whole process table every poll; PSI corroborates and never gates (ADR-0009). Its default action is `--report`.

cgroup_root.description: The cgroup v2 directory holding the per-user slices. PSI is read at the slice, never per scope (ADR-0003).

slice_prefix.description: The prefix of a per-user slice directory name; the uid sits between prefix and suffix.

slice_suffix.description: The suffix of a per-user slice directory name.

origins.description: Ordered `{pattern, label}` pairs mapping a process's cgroup leaf name to a descriptive origin; first match wins, no match is `other`. Add one per ssh transport or container runtime the site runs. Origin never feeds the kill decision (ADR-0003).

pattern.description: A Python regular expression matched against the cgroup leaf name (the last path component), never the full path.

label.description: The origin label recorded in the finding, lower-case with underscores.

traversal_budget_s.description: How long a traversal may have been running before it is a finding. Age is one of the process-table facts; it is never inferred from PSI.

fanout_n.description: How many concurrent traversals under one effective parent count as a fan-out finding, the shape of a parallelised walk.

io_stall_fraction.description: The differenced `io.pressure` `full` fraction over one poll window above which a user slice is marked `stalling_slice: true`. Calibrate from the differenced rate under known load, never from cumulative totals (ADR-0002).

cpu_stall_fraction.description: The differenced `cpu.pressure` fraction over one poll window that marks a slice as stalling. Corroborating only; it never suppresses a record (ADR-0009).

kill_grace_s.description: Seconds between `SIGTERM` and `SIGKILL` under `--kill`. After the kill the reaper re-checks and records `signalled_but_wedged` if the process is still there.

max_kills.description: The most processes one poll may signal. A poll that wants more stops and reports; a runaway reaper is its own incident.

settle_s.description: Seconds the reaper waits after its last signal before re-reading the process table to decide what actually died.

audit_max_bytes.description: Rotate the audit file when it exceeds this size. The floor is one mebibyte so rotation cannot be set to thrash.

stream_filters.description: Commands whose stdin the reaper senses (ADR-0011): a long-lived one of these reading from an expensive mount is a finding of a different shape from a walk.

timer.description: The reaper's systemd timer. This node is shared; the slot is chosen against the live schedule of the target node and never copied from an example.

on_calendar.description: The `OnCalendar=` expression. Survey the live schedule first (`systemctl list-timers --all` as root, and every account's `systemctl --user list-timers`) and pick a minute AND a second clear of every neighbour; a per-minute collector leaves the second field as the only separation. Checked with `systemd-analyze calendar` at build when available.

randomized_delay_sec.description: `RandomizedDelaySec=`. Zero by default: a deliberately chosen slot is undone by jitter, so widen this only when the schedule has no clear slot.

accuracy_sec.description: `AccuracySec=`. Tight by default so the timer fires in the slot that was chosen rather than coalescing onto a neighbour.

persistent.description: `Persistent=`. Off by default: a missed poll is not worth a catch-up run at an unplanned second on a shared node.

timeout_start_sec.description: `TimeoutStartSec=` for the reaper service. Must be at least the floor derived from the relink and kill budgets, so systemd never cuts a poll off mid-kill.

relink_timeout_s.description: Seconds the reconcile's link-farm and hook re-check may take before it is abandoned. It reports and never repairs (ADR-0008).

relink_kill_after_s.description: Grace after `relink_timeout_s` before the reconcile is killed outright. The reaper's own poll runs regardless: a Layer 1 diagnosis must not stop the Layer 2 backstop.
